prompt: Are there limitatiions to a systematic review that included literature of studies made both before and after covid
judge_reasoning: All candidates address limitations in the broad sense of pandemic-era evidence, but Candidate [3] most directly targets the core issue of integrating studies collected both before and after COVID-19 in a systematic review (e.g., changes in data collection, patient behavior, healthcare systems, selection bias, and temporal effects). Candidate [1] is also strongly on-topic, but it is slightly more generic and less focused on the specific pre/post integration confounders than [3]. Candidate [4] is relevant yet more framed as meta-analysis across time periods and covers fewer of the integration-specific threats. Candidate [2] is the least aligned because it discusses post-COVID systematic-review quality and broader publication/review dynamics rather than the specific challenges of combining pre- and post-pandemic studies.
